exposure: second-stage cesarean delivery with failed vacuum-assisted extraction
second-stage cesarean delivery without a trial of vacuum-assisted extraction
History of second-stage cesarean delivery with failed vacuum-assisted extraction vs. without a trial of vacuum-assisted extraction
outcome: Preterm delivery (<37, <34, <32, and <28 weeks of gestation)
cohort: Women in their subsequent pregnancy after a second-stage cesarean delivery
finding: A history of failed vacuum-assisted delivery during a previous second-stage cesarean delivery was associated with a higher risk of preterm delivery at <37 weeks of gestation in the subsequent birth.
mod_finding: This study examined the maternal and neonatal outcomes of women who had a second-stage cesarean delivery, comparing those with a prior failed vacuum-assisted delivery to those without.
